sentences.text: Sidney H. Haughton named this dinosaur in 1915.
The genus name honors Kangnas farm, while the species name coetzeei recognizes the farmer Coetzee.
The holotype, which is the specimen the species is based on, is a single tooth recovered from a well.
Haughton also described other fossils that might belong to the animal, such as partial thigh bones, shin bones, a metatarsal, vertebrae, and unidentified bones.
Like other basal iguanodontians, Kangnasaurus would have been a bipedal herbivore.
Recent research places Kangnasaurus within the elasmarian group.
Although many experts view it as a dubious genus, a 2007 review by Ruiz-Omeñaca and colleagues kept it as potentially valid.
Remains date between the middle-Campanian and Maastrichtian periods.
Sedimentological analyses suggest a Late Cretaceous age between the Campanian and Maastrichtian is more likely than an Early Cretaceous age.
Some sources suggest Kangnasaurus lived at the beginning of the Cretaceous period, approximately 134 million years ago during the Valanginian, in what is now Africa.
The Paleobiology Database lists the time range for Kangnasaurus as Cenomanian to Maastrichtian (100.5 to 66 million years ago).
It is debated whether additional fossils described by Haughton and Cooper actually belong to Kangnasaurus, as some bones may have come from other deposits.
